name: Calendar
baseMeaning: A calendar icon, signaling time-coded moment, schedule-coded affection, or 'save the date' energy.
tldr: 📅 marks a date or plan; with 💍, it can announce an engagement and call for a save-the-date.

contextMeanings.meaning: 📅 identifies a specific day on which an event, plan, or deadline will happen.
📅 gives a quick, practical acknowledgment that a date has been chosen.
📅💍 presents the chosen date as part of an engagement announcement.
📅 points to the scheduled day for a meeting, launch, review, or other fixed milestone.

platformNotes.note: In a private iMessage thread, 📅 is useful shorthand for confirming a date with a partner, friend, or relative. Adding 💍 makes an engagement announcement much clearer than the calendar alone.
On TikTok, a standalone 📅 may seem to point toward a date, event, or scheduled release mentioned nearby. Its meaning still depends heavily on the caption and any other emoji used with it.
WhatsApp conversations often use 📅 to organize family meals, trips, and celebrations. In a wedding thread, 📅💍 reads as a formal save-the-date message rather than a casual date reminder.
In Slack, 📅 is usually read as a lightweight schedule marker when the surrounding text identifies the meeting or deadline. It works best when the actual date and commitment are already explicit.

generationalNotes.note: A bare 📅 often works as quick shorthand for locking in a plan, particularly when the conversation already makes the date clear.
Millennials may read 📅 as practical planning language, especially when organizing weddings, family events, or trips.
Gen X recipients may take 📅 more literally as a calendar reminder or formal date marker rather than as casual emotional punctuation.

warnings.title: The engagement gets lost
warnings.description: In a save-the-date exchange, 📅 alone may be understood only as a date reminder. If the engagement itself matters, pair it with 💍 and name the occasion in words.

seoDescription: What does 📅 mean? It marks a date or planned event, and with 💍 it can announce an engagement and invite everyone to save the date.

longForm.overview:
The 📅 calendar emoji begins as a quick answer to a moment built around timing. A friend mentions a trip, someone names a day for lunch, or a partner asks whether a date is happening; 📅 can say “put that in your calendar” without turning the message into a formal invitation. Alone, it is pointed toward the date or plan, not necessarily toward the relationship attached to it.

Its meaning becomes more specific when it joins another symbol. In a save-the-date message, 📅💍 marks both the date and the engagement, with the calendar doing the date-setting work and the ring making the occasion explicit. By contrast, 📅 on its own can be read as practical acknowledgment or as a date reminder, so people may use a little more context when they need clarity. 📅 is not a universal stand-in for romance: what matters is whether the conversation is about a schedule, a celebration, or the relationship behind it. The surrounding words and nearby emoji decide which meaning lands, rather than the calendar icon acting as a fixed romantic signal.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
📅 tends to arrive when timing needs to become concrete. “What are we doing Saturday?” can be answered with “that day 📅”; a friend who has settled on a party date may send “saving the date 📅”; or a couple can use 📅💍 to make both the chosen day and the engagement explicit. The bare emoji is often the first, low-friction response from someone organizing the plan, rather than a grand announcement.

It also shows up as light shorthand in social plans, family gatherings, and reminders. In those chats, it usually means “that date matters, remember it.” It carries less relationship meaning than 📅💍 and less celebration than 🎉💍. If the sender wants the warmth of the engagement acknowledged, the reply can name the occasion rather than leaving every participant to infer it.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
📅💍 is a poor substitute for clearly describing an engagement. If the relationship news matters, send the words; the combination can confirm a save-the-date message, but a bare 📅 may be understood only as a date reminder. Likewise, do not rely on 📅 to turn vague flirting into a confirmed plan, because the emoji can simply mark scheduling.

In professional messages, plain dates are usually clearer than emoji shorthand. Use 📅 when the day is already obvious and the tone is casual, not when the recipient needs to distinguish a deadline from a meeting or an informal idea from a firm commitment. In family or wedding exchanges, check the surrounding symbols: 📅💍 explicitly joins date and engagement, while 📅 by itself leaves more room for interpretation.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends a bare 📅, confirm the useful part: “what day are we talking?” or “saving it 📅.” When the message announces an engagement, match the more specific warmth with “can’t wait 💍🎊,” or use 📅💍 if you want to repeat the formal save-the-date signal. The calendar is often practical first; adding a ring or celebration emoji tells the sender you understood the occasion.

If 📅 lands on your own message and the date feels vague, ask for the exact day. If it seems to announce an engagement, respond to the news directly rather than replying only with a generic reaction. That prevents a date acknowledgment from sounding like you noticed the timing but missed what the date means.

faqs.question: What does 📅 mean from a guy
faqs.answer: It usually means he is pointing to a date or making a concrete plan. It does not, by itself, prove romantic interest; nearby words or 💍 determine that.

faqs.question: Is 📅 flirty
faqs.answer: It can be when it accompanies a date idea or an engagement announcement, but the calendar by itself is mostly about timing. Add 💍 when the relationship context needs to be explicit.

faqs.question: What does 📅 mean on TikTok
faqs.answer: In a comment or caption, it may mark a mentioned date, event, or plan. If the post is about an engagement, 📅💍 makes the save-the-date meaning clearer.

faqs.question: Can I use 📅 for save the date
faqs.answer: Yes. A bare 📅 marks the date, while 📅💍 combines that date with an explicit engagement signal. Clear words are still useful when the recipient might not recognize the emoji combination.

conversationExamples.message: we finally picked our wedding day 📅💍
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a formal engagement-and-date announcement. Reply with warm recognition such as “can’t wait 💍🎊” rather than treating it like an ordinary reminder.
The sender has settled the date and wants friends to remember it. A practical answer like “saving it 📅” fits, or ask what to bring.
The calendar identifies the new working day. Confirm the time and scope directly, especially if the original schedule changed.

conversationExamples.message: we set the date for the reception 📅💍
conversationExamples.interpretation: The date and engagement are being announced together. Family members can respond with celebration or acknowledge the practical details.

conversationExamples.message: museum trip is happening next sunday 📅
conversationExamples.interpretation: This is a casual plan with a fixed day. Answer with the calendar emoji to confirm or ask about the meeting time.
